1: # Optional unconditional formalization
2: 
3: `--track full --formalization unconditional` selects
4: `2basis -> shared NL0/Audit A -> shared nl02lean/Audit B -> b2lean`.
5: The default is `conditional`; `full` still means both existing stages, not an
6: unconditional theorem. Existing jobs without `formalization` remain conditional.
7: Unconditional entry starts before NL0: accepted NL0 cannot skip the required
8: original-target/basis Audit A through `translate`.
9: 
10: ## Authority
11: 
12: The original selected target and documents remain immutable authority for H,
13: quantifiers, domains, parameters, normalizations, constant dependencies and any
14: specified algorithm. 2basis may change the proof route and representations.
15: The model chooses mathematical reductions. Python checks records, versions,
16: actual Lean proofs and interfaces; it does not certify source fidelity.
17: No difficulty scores, forced reduction tree or Mathlib-use whitelist apply.
18: 
19: One subsequent Audit A receives original documents, `basis-proof.md`, complete
20: `basis-registry.json`, retained source evidence and `proof-context.json`.
21: Its global lane checks original-target fidelity, replacement dependencies and
22: structure; ordinary local R lanes check all new arguments. There is no preceding
23: full mathematical audit of 2basis. NL0 faithfully presents the active basis route,
24: without requiring the original proof route to remain unchanged. Review reuse
25: includes active context; source warnings retain their original qualification.
26: 
27: ## Submission schema
28: 
29: Submit an object with exactly:
30: 
31: ```text
32: version: "yui-basis-1"
33: full_target: exact target-selection.json full_target
34: proof: complete basis-reduced natural-language proof
35: lean_header: "import Mathlib\n" followed by needed object definitions
36: dependencies: [dependency, ...]
37: replacements: [{original_dependency, replacement:[B IDs], explanation}, ...]
38: ```
39: 
40: Each dependency has exactly:
41: 
42: ```text
43: id: B001 (three or more digits)
44: category: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
45: statement: complete mathematical statement
46: origin: {kind, reference, revision, evidence:[evidence reference, ...]}
47: compatibility: native | adapted | internal | unresolved
48: uses: [other B IDs]
49: port: E001 | M001 | null
50: lean: {type: closed Lean proposition, proof: tactic body after "by"} | null
51: justification: actual source/reduction/compatibility account
52: ```
53: 
54: Origin kinds are `mathlib`, `lean-library`, `derivation`, `textbook`, respectively.
55: Reference identifies the actual declaration/public source/theorem or derivation;
56: revision identifies its version/edition. Category and compatibility are distinct:
57: a Mathlib result from another version is still class 1, possibly `adapted`.
58: 
59: - Class 1/native: direct Mathlib (`port:null`) or optional M port.
60: - Class 1/adapted and class 2: provisional E port with actual checked proof in
61:   the pinned target environment. Prepare needed adapters and retained source
62:   attribution now; no whole-library migration prerequisite.
63: - Class 3: `internal`, `port:null`, `lean:null`, nonempty `uses`. Give a concrete
64:   derivation in the proof, recursively from 1/2 via other 3, with no unresolved
65:   4. Existing NL0/T workers prove it internally; it cannot become an E premise.
66: - Class 4: `unresolved`, E port, `lean:{type,proof:null}`. Retain a verified
67:   complete textbook theorem and evidence. Missing sources, contradictions,
68:   unspecified statements and internal proof gaps are not 4.
69: 
70: `uses` records genuine dependencies; unknown IDs and cycles are rejected.
71: Prepared 1/2 proofs may refer to other prepared 1/2 proofs as `YuiBasis.Bddd`.
72: Their closed types bind their own parameters/typeclasses, without project H/E.
73: Use inline local Lean constructions for private helpers. All used 1/2 proofs
74: must compile and pass dependency/axiom inspection in 2basis. The header contains
75: object definitions, not axioms, theorem declarations or executable metaprogramming.
76: 
77: Evidence is `{input:"declared-document-ID"}` or an actual retained own-stage
78: `{path,sha256}`. Class 4 requires evidence. References bind actual bytes;
79: the basis reviewer checks source completeness and classification before release. The shared Audit A also reviews the actual later uses.
80: 
81: Use `base_candidate:N` with JSON-pointer patches into the basis object, or
82: `accept_candidate:N`. `base_input:"prior-basis.json"` continues user-requested
83: reduction. Every revised artifact receives the same real native checks.
84: Compiler/resource nonpass is feedback, not mathematical impossibility.
85: 
86: For long reductions, `save_basis_draft` saves partial work without running Lean;
87: `read_basis_draft` reads only that author's actual saved candidates, with bounded
88: JSON-pointer pagination. A context-reset checkpoint names the newest draft and
89: last machine-checked candidate separately. Saving does not make a proof complete.
90: 
91: ## Early statement and use review
92: 
93: Only a submitted, machine-checked basis enters the separate basis reviewer role.
94: It compares classes 1, 2 and 4 together against the original sources, the
95: rewritten use and the propositions printed by Lean. For class 4 it reads the
96: value of the proposition definition. The comparison covers quantifier order,
97: uniform constants, domains, assumptions, direction, definitions and adapters.
98: Class 3 derivations go to the ordinary NL0 and Lean workers.
99: 
100: The reviewer submits a located PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIED for every assigned item.
101: A normal-policy nonpass goes back to the same basis author with the prior
102: artifact and findings. First-pass policy retains the first nonpass. Saving or
103: checking drafts costs no reviewer call. Each submitted revision uses at most
104: one review batch. An empty scope uses zero calls. Exact previous assessments
105: can be reused within the case when their sources, rules, shared route and
106: connected dependencies and uses still match. Unchanged rejected work retains
107: its findings and pauses. The execution ledger includes both roles.
108: 
109: The active context binds the selected basis, native check and semantic report.
110: Downstream readback verifies their inputs and the reviewer's complete submission.
111: Historical native-only contexts use their original runtime snapshots.
112: 
113: ## Remaining class 4 and errors
114: 
115: The existing retained controller records an exact `basis-decision` incident.
116: Only explicit user choices authorize these commands:
117: 
118: ```sh
119: python3 -B nl0/scripts/yui.py basis-decision RUN --incident ID --action stop
120: python3 -B nl0/scripts/yui.py basis-decision RUN --incident ID --action continue
121: python3 -B nl0/scripts/yui.py basis-decision RUN --incident ID --action accept-conditional
122: ```
123: 
124: Continue retains the author/prior artifact. Accept binds exact residual IDs and
125: artifact, without approving future additions. Stop records an unfinished
126: user-stopped outcome and releases owned roles. The batch reads its incident and
127: control after case exit and admits the next queued case. A case deadline also
128: applies while the operator choice is pending. Stale/changed/dead-owner decisions
129: are rejected. No silent conditional fallback.
130: 
131: Transport faults, cancellation, budgets and native limits use existing handling.
132: Unexpected faults retain evidence at PAUSED_ERROR, without authorizing cleanup
133: of real runs. Test cleanup is a separate test-only boundary.
134: 
135: ## Explicit revision of a downstream basis defect
136: 
137: If a global NL0 or interface role finds a conflict in a frozen B statement or
138: Lean type, use `report_basis_defect`. Identify the exact field and value, quote
139: the original source and the affected use, and explain the correction. A local
140: proof worker can send a connection problem through its existing diagnosis
141: route. The global reporting stage checks the citations against the documents it
142: was given. A valid report pauses the case as `BASIS_REVISION_REQUIRED`.
143: 
144: Inspect the finding before choosing a revision. To continue, cancel the paused
145: case, wait for the case and its worker processes to exit, then run
146: 
147: ```sh
148: python3 -B nl0/scripts/yui.py resume RUN --repair-basis --prepare-only
149: python3 -B nl0/scripts/yui.py execute NEW_RUN
150: ```
151: 
152: The new job starts from the previous basis and the located objection under the
153: original target, profiles, policy, worker limit and deadline. The prior run keeps
154: its evidence and costs. The revised basis must pass the native and correspondence
155: checks, including a response to the objection for a retained formal item. New
156: NL0, Audit A, interface, proof and final checks follow. If the old round had
157: completed local Lean bodies, an identical local program and use context may
158: supply a candidate after the new interface freeze. The proof queue checks it
159: with the current kernel before skipping a worker. Audit A's whole-context
160: binding invalidates the previous acceptance. Any new residual choice requires
161: its own operator decision.
162: 
163: ## Shared translation and final closure
164: 
165: The interface author receives prepared basis header/E types. Preserve that
166: header prefix and exact E types; independently review the NL/Lean correspondence
167: before freezing. Original H and whole target retain ordinary semantic review.
168: All shared proof, repair, assembly and worker machinery is reused.
169: 
170: After machine Audit B, b2lean applies prepared 1/2 proofs to `AuditBExport.P` and
171: generates `YuiClosed.P`, with only H and explicitly approved 4. Compile the final
172: standalone source and inspect its actual full signature and transitive trust.
173: An old conditional receipt cannot establish final closure. No final NL model.
174: Missing proofs, extra premises, signature/source/version drift, unexpected axioms
175: or incomplete inspection fail acceptance.
176: An exception with unconfirmed native shutdown retains a marked workspace and
177: diagnostic for owned cleanup; normal completed native checks release scratch.
178: 
179: `b2lean/Proof.lean`, `check.json` and `report.json` bind the final export.
180: Only closed output with unqualified upstream authority is `UNCONDITIONAL_LEAN`
181: and `WORKFLOW-PASSED`. Approved 4 yields `CONDITIONAL_LEAN`. A closed kernel proof
182: with remaining source qualifications is `CLOSED_LEAN_SOURCE_QUALIFIED`, with
183: `closure.kernel_closed:true` but no unconditional workflow acceptance. Both
184: qualified cases remain `WORKFLOW-CONDITIONAL`, with warnings and an unmet
185: unconditional goal. Interface drift cannot inherit exact frozen closure.

1: # Hausdorff dimension of a product with an interval
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
6: Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
7: Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
8: Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).
9: 
10: > 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
11: > \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
12: > \(\mathbb R\).
13: 
14: ## Fixed interpretation and complete target
15: 
16: Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
17: 2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
18: \(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
19: the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.
20: 
21: Let \(n\geq0\) be an integer, let \(E\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty
22: compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)
23: with \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) and use its Euclidean metric. Prove
24: 
25: \[
26: \dim_H(E\times[0,1])=\dim_H E+1.
27: \]
28: 
29: The zero-dimensional ambient space \(\mathbb R^0\) is included. A later
30: formalization using a different product norm must justify the metric change.
31: 
32: ## Fixed natural-language proof
33: 
34: For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put
35: 
36: \[
37: H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
38:  A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
39: \qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
40: \]
41: 
42: Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero. This
43: unnormalized Hausdorff measure gives the usual Hausdorff dimension. We use
44: its critical-exponent characterization: \(H^s(A)=0\) if
45: \(s>\dim_H A\), and \(H^s(A)=\infty\) if \(0<s<\dim_H A\).
46: Conversely, zero measure implies \(\dim_H A\leq s\), and infinite
47: measure implies \(\dim_H A\geq s\).
48: 
49: Write \(D=\dim_H E\) and \(F=E\times[0,1]\). First \(0\leq D\leq n\).
50: Indeed, compactness makes \(E\) bounded. When \(n>0\), a box containing
51: it admits a cover by at most \(Ch^{-n}\) cubes of side at most \(h\),
52: for \(0<h\leq1\). Here \(C\) depends only on that box. Each cube has
53: diameter at most \(\sqrt n h\). For any \(s>n\), the total \(s\)-cost
54: is at most \(C n^{s/2}h^{s-n}\to0\). These arbitrarily fine covers
55: give \(H^s(E)=0\) and hence \(D\leq n\). If \(n=0\), nonemptiness
56: makes \(E=\mathbb R^0\), a singleton of zero \(s\)-cost for every
57: \(s>0\); thus \(D=0\).
58: 
59: ### Upper bound
60: 
61: When \(n=0\), \(F\) is isometric to \([0,1]\). Dividing this interval
62: into \(N\) equal pieces gives total \(a\)-cost \(N^{1-a}\to0\) for
63: every \(a>1\), proving \(\dim_H F\leq1=D+1\).
64: For this upper-bound argument now assume \(n\geq1\).
65: 
66: Fix \(q>D\). Since \(q>0\) and \(H^q(E)=0\), for every
67: \(0<r\leq1\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a countable cover
68: \((U_i)\) of \(E\) with nonempty-member diameters
69: \(0<r_i\leq r\) and \(\sum_i r_i^q<\varepsilon\).
70: The positive-diameter requirement costs nothing: start with a cover of
71: cost below \(\varepsilon/2\); replace each zero-diameter singleton by
72: a ball of diameter at most \(r\), choosing the \(i\)-th replacement
73: to have \(q\)-cost less than \(\varepsilon2^{-i-2}\). The added cost
74: is less than \(\varepsilon/2\). Discard empty members.
75: 
76: Let \(N_i=\lceil1/r_i\rceil\). Partition \([0,1]\) into \(N_i\)
77: closed intervals of length \(1/N_i\leq r_i\). Because \(r_i\leq1\),
78: \(N_i\leq2/r_i\). The corresponding products with \(U_i\) form a
79: countable cover of \(F\). Each has Euclidean diameter at most
80: \(\sqrt2 r_i\), and their total \((q+1)\)-cost is at most
81: 
82: \[
83: \sum_iN_i(\sqrt2 r_i)^{q+1}
84: \leq2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\sum_i r_i^q
85: <2(\sqrt2)^{q+1}\varepsilon.
86: \]
87: 
88: For any target scale \(\delta>0\), choose
89: \(r\leq\min(1,\delta/\sqrt2)\), then let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
90: Thus \(H^{q+1}_\delta(F)=0\) for every scale, so
91: \(H^{q+1}(F)=0\) and \(\dim_H F\leq q+1\). Letting \(q\downarrow D\)
92: gives \(\dim_H F\leq D+1\).
93: 
94: ### Lower bound when \(D>0\)
95: 
96: Fix \(0<s<D\). Then \(H^s(E)=\infty\), so
97: \(H^s_\delta(E)\) becomes arbitrarily large as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
98: We claim that, for every \(\delta>0\),
99: 
100: \[
101: H^s_\delta(E)\leq H^{s+1}_\delta(F).                 \tag{1}
102: \]
103: 
104: Take an arbitrary countable \(\delta\)-cover \((V_i)_{i\geq0}\) of
105: \(F\), discarding empty members. Define
106: \(\rho_i=\operatorname{diam}V_i\),
107: \(A_i=\pi_{\mathbb R^n}(V_i)\), and
108: \(B_i=\pi_{\mathbb R}(V_i)\). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz,
109: so both projected diameters are at most \(\rho_i\leq\delta\).
110: For \(\varepsilon>0\), put
111: 
112: \[
113: \eta_i=\frac{\varepsilon2^{-i-1}}{1+\rho_i^s}>0.
114: \]
115: 
116: Enclose \(B_i\) in an open interval \(J_i\) of length at most
117: \(\rho_i+\eta_i\): its supremum minus infimum is at most \(\rho_i\),
118: and an enlargement of total width \(\eta_i\) suffices. This avoids
119: assuming that the arbitrary covering sets or their projections are measurable.
120: 
121: For each \(t\in[0,1]\), the sets \(A_i\) for which \(t\in J_i\)
122: cover \(E\). Indeed, a point \((x,t)\in F\) belongs to some \(V_i\),
123: giving \(x\in A_i\) and \(t\in B_i\subset J_i\). Their diameters
124: are at most \(\rho_i\). Consequently, with \(c=H^s_\delta(E)\),
125: 
126: \[
127: c\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s\mathbf1_{J_i}(t)\quad(t\in[0,1]).
128: \]
129: 
130: The constant \(c\) is finite: compactness gives a finite cover of \(E\)
131: by balls of diameter at most \(\delta\), with finite \(s\)-cost.
132: Each summand is nonnegative and measurable since \(J_i\) is open.
133: Integrate over \([0,1]\), of Lebesgue measure one, and use Tonelli's
134: theorem for this nonnegative series. Since
135: \(|J_i\cap[0,1]|\leq\rho_i+\eta_i\),
136: 
137: \[
138: \begin{aligned}
139: c&\leq\sum_i\rho_i^s|J_i\cap[0,1]|\\
140:  &\leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\sum_i\eta_i\rho_i^s
141:  \leq\sum_i\rho_i^{s+1}+\varepsilon.
142: \end{aligned}
143: \]
144: 
145: If the first series is infinite the desired inequality is immediate;
146: otherwise let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). Take the infimum over the
147: arbitrary covers to obtain (1). As its left side is unbounded at small
148: scales, \(H^{s+1}(F)=\infty\), giving \(\dim_H F\geq s+1\).
149: Letting \(s\uparrow D\) proves \(\dim_H F\geq D+1\).
150: 
151: ### Lower bound when \(D=0\)
152: 
153: Choose \(x_0\in E\). The map \(t\mapsto(x_0,t)\) is an isometric
154: embedding of \([0,1]\) into \(F\), so dimension monotonicity gives
155: \(\dim_H F\geq\dim_H[0,1]\). This interval has dimension one:
156: equal-length covers gave the upper bound above. For \(0<s<1\), any
157: \(\delta\)-cover with diameters \(\rho_i\leq\delta\) satisfies
158: \(\sum_i\rho_i\geq1\). To see this, enclose its nonempty members
159: in open intervals of lengths at most \(\rho_i+\varepsilon2^{-i-1}\),
160: use countable subadditivity of length to get
161: \(1\leq\sum_i\rho_i+\varepsilon\), and let \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
162: Hence \(\sum_i\rho_i^s\geq\delta^{s-1}\sum_i\rho_i
163: \geq\delta^{s-1}\to\infty\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
164: This proves the lower bound one. Thus \(\dim_H F\geq1=D+1\),
165: including when \(n=0\).
166: 
167: Together the bounds establish the required equality.

13: # Hausdorff dimension
14: 
15: The Hausdorff dimension of a set `X` in an (extended) metric space is the unique number
16: `dimH s : ℝ≥0∞` such that for any `d : ℝ≥0` we have
17: 
18: - `μH[d] s = 0` if `dimH s < d`, and
19: - `μH[d] s = ∞` if `d < dimH s`.
20: 
21: In this file we define `dimH s` to be the Hausdorff dimension of `s`, then prove some basic
22: properties of Hausdorff dimension.
23: 
24: ## Main definitions
25: 
26: * `MeasureTheory.dimH`: the Hausdorff dimension of a set. For the Hausdorff dimension of the whole
27:   space we use `MeasureTheory.dimH (Set.univ : Set X)`.
28: 
29: ## Main results
30: 
31: ### Basic properties of Hausdorff dimension
32: 
33: * `hausdorffMeasure_of_lt_dimH`, `dimH_le_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_top`,
34:   `le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_eq_top`, `hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt`, `measure_zero_of_dimH_lt`,
35:   `le_dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero`, `dimH_of_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero_ne_top`: various forms
36:   of the characteristic property of the Hausdorff dimension;
37: * `dimH_union`: the Hausdorff dimension of the union of two sets is the maximum of their Hausdorff
38:   dimensions.
39: * `dimH_iUnion`, `dimH_bUnion`, `dimH_sUnion`: the Hausdorff dimension of a countable union of sets
40:   is the supremum of their Hausdorff dimensions;
41: * `dimH_empty`, `dimH_singleton`, `Set.Subsingleton.dimH_zero`, `Set.Countable.dimH_zero` : `dimH s
42:   = 0` whenever `s` is countable;
43: 
44: ### (Pre)images under (anti)lipschitz and Hölder continuous maps
45: 
46: * `HolderWith.dimH_image_le` etc: if `f : X → Y` is Hölder continuous with exponent `r > 0`, then
47:   for any `s`, `dimH (f '' s) ≤ dimH s / r`. We prove versions of this statement for `HolderWith`,
48:   `HolderOnWith`, and locally Hölder maps, as well as for `Set.image` and `Set.range`.
49: * `LipschitzWith.dimH_image_le` etc: Lipschitz continuous maps do not increase the Hausdorff
50:   dimension of sets.
51: * for a map that is known to be both Lipschitz and antilipschitz (e.g., for an `Isometry` or
52:   a `ContinuousLinearEquiv`) we also prove `dimH (f '' s) = dimH s`.
53: 
54: ### Hausdorff measure in `ℝⁿ`
55: 
56: * `Real.dimH_of_nonempty_interior`: if `s` is a set in a finite-dimensional real vector space `E`
57:   with nonempty interior, then the Hausdorff dimension of `s` is equal to the dimension of `E`.
58: * `dense_compl_of_dimH_lt_finrank`: if `s` is a set in a finite-dimensional real vector space `E`
59:   with Hausdorff dimension strictly less than the dimension of `E`, the `s` has a dense complement.
60: * `ContDiff.dense_compl_range_of_finrank_lt_finrank`: the complement to the range of a `C¹`
61:   smooth map is dense provided that the dimension of the domain is strictly less than the dimension
62:   of the codomain.
63: 
64: ## Notation
65: 
66: We use the following notation localized in `MeasureTheory`. It is defined in
67: `MeasureTheory.Measure.Hausdorff`.
68: 
69: - `μH[d]` : `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure d`
70: 
71: ## Implementation notes
72: 
73: * The definition of `dimH` explicitly uses `borel X` as a measurable space structure. This way we
74:   can formulate lemmas about Hausdorff dimension without assuming that the environment has a
75:   `[MeasurableSpace X]` instance that is equal but possibly not defeq to `borel X`.
76: 
77:   Lemma `dimH_def` unfolds this definition using whatever `[MeasurableSpace X]` instance we have in
78:   the environment (as long as it is equal to `borel X`).
79: 
80: * The definition `dimH` is irreducible; use API lemmas or `dimH_def` instead.
81:

15: # Hausdorff measure and metric (outer) measures
16: 
17: In this file we define the `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure on an (extended) metric space `X` and
18: the Hausdorff dimension of a set in an (extended) metric space. Let `μ d δ` be the maximal outer
19: measure such that `μ d δ s ≤ (ediam s) ^ d` for every set of diameter less than `δ`. Then
20: the Hausdorff measure `μH[d] s` of `s` is defined as `⨆ δ > 0, μ d δ s`. By Carathéodory's theorem
21: `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.borel_le_caratheodory`, this is a Borel measure on `X`.
22: 
23: The value of `μH[d]`, `d > 0`, on a set `s` (measurable or not) is given by
24: ```
25: μH[d] s = ⨆ (r : ℝ≥0∞) (hr : 0 < r), ⨅ (t : ℕ → Set X) (hts : s ⊆ ⋃ n, t n)
26:     (ht : ∀ n, ediam (t n) ≤ r), ∑' n, ediam (t n) ^ d
27: ```
28: 
29: For every set `s` and any `d < d'` we have either `μH[d] s = ∞` or `μH[d'] s = 0`, see
30: `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top`. In
31: `Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/HausdorffDimension.lean` we use this fact to define the Hausdorff
32: dimension `dimH` of a set in an (extended) metric space.
33: 
34: We also define two generalizations of the Hausdorff measure. In one generalization (see
35: `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric`) we take any function `m (diam s)` instead of `(diam s) ^ d`. In
36: an even more general definition (see `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric'`) we use any function
37: of `m : Set X → ℝ≥0∞`. Some authors start with a partial function `m` defined only on some sets
38: `s : Set X` (e.g., only on balls or only on measurable sets). This is equivalent to our definition
39: applied to `MeasureTheory.extend m`.
40: 
41: We also define a predicate `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric` which says that an outer measure
42: is additive on metric separated pairs of sets: `μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t` provided that
43: `⨅ (x ∈ s) (y ∈ t), edist x y ≠ 0`. This is the property required for Carathéodory's theorem
44: `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.borel_le_caratheodory`, so we prove this theorem for any
45: metric outer measure, then prove that outer measures constructed using `mkMetric'` are metric outer
46: measures.
47: 
48: ## Main definitions
49: 
50: * `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric`: an outer measure `μ` is called *metric* if
51:   `μ (s ∪ t) = μ s + μ t` for any two metric separated sets `s` and `t`. A metric outer measure in a
52:   Borel extended metric space is guaranteed to satisfy the Carathéodory condition, see
53:   `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.IsMetric.borel_le_caratheodory`.
54: * `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.mkMetric'` and its particular case
55:   `MeasureTheory.OuterMeasure.mkMetric`: a construction of an outer measure that is guaranteed to
56:   be metric. Both constructions are generalizations of the Hausdorff measure. The same measures
57:   interpreted as Borel measures are called `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric'` and
58:   `MeasureTheory.Measure.mkMetric`.
59: * `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure` a.k.a. `μH[d]`: the `d`-dimensional Hausdorff measure.
60:   There are many definitions of the Hausdorff measure that differ from each other by a
61:   multiplicative constant. We put

69: ### Basic properties

87: * `MeasureTheory.hausdorffMeasure_pi_real`: for a nonempty `ι`, `μH[card ι]` on `ι → ℝ` equals

1: # Self-containment details
2: 
3: This details the statement/object and dependency/scope requirements grouped
4: under Audit A's statement_closure and dependency_closure criteria. The
5: [shared Audit A section](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
6: is the acceptance authority for author and auditor; this annex supplies
7: interpretation and examples, not an independent permission policy.
8: 
9: ## Two boundaries
10: 
11: Accepted NL0 is a complete proof relative to its declared H/E/M roots, frozen
12: logical foundation and version-bound mathematically reviewed background notes. It is not an outline requiring the original manuscript to
13: recover missing definitions, formulas, assumptions, or arguments. E/M statements
14: are fully restated; their primary sources are inspected for provenance, not
15: used to supply unstated premises. The fixed library's own proof dependencies
16: need not be recopied. The target work's internal results must be proved here.
17: 
18: Every R must also be checkable from its packet alone: the complete statements
19: of its direct inputs, their required definitions/declarations, its complete
20: output, its local declarations, and its own argument. Another R's proof body,
21: an ancestor not listed as an input, an ambient original H, an original-source
22: crosswalk, or remembered material is not an additional mathematical resource.
23: Whole-target/source-fidelity checks are separate from this local proof check.
24: Under mathematical-background-v2-1, a reviewer may positively assess routine
25: local mathematical facts and record precise statements, available conditions
26: and justification. Exact Mathlib bindings are deferred to nl02lean; no native
27: query is required for ordinary background. These notes add neither H nor a
28: core proof route. Mathematical uncertainty still blocks. See
29: [background notes](background-notes.md).
30: 
31: Original theorem conditions are H nodes, including conditions that could be
32: encoded in a refined type. Parameters introduce ambient data/structures, not
33: an ambient stock of original hypotheses. For example, declare a vector and
34: put its required nonzero condition in H; do not write “nonzero vector” in its
35: parameter type and use that condition from an empty input list. The same rule
36: applies to characteristic/range conditions and equations. An R must list every
37: original H it actually uses. Standard structure operations/axioms and the fixed
38: finite-language rules remain available; no new substantive theorem is added.
39: 
40: An output must be understandable and callable without reading its producer's
41: argument. Include the actual equalities/inequalities, binder types, hypotheses,
42: parameter windows, constant dependencies, representatives and a.e./pointwise
43: meaning. Global defined notation can be expanded from the packet. A formula
44: number, theorem name, or paragraph location cannot replace mathematical content.
45: Source locators belong in provenance fields. New mathematical prose uses direct
46: input IDs and previously proved local F IDs, not inherited numbered references.
47: 
48: ## Object closure
49: 
50: For every mathematical object actually appearing in a statement, definition,
51: local declaration, or proof, locate one legitimate declaration:
52: 
53: 1. A frozen parameter, explicit logical primitive, or global D definition.
54:    State its meaning, type/domain and parameter dependence. Global primitives
55:    cover only core typed syntax, not a dictionary of subject-specific objects.
56:    New subjects use the same parameter/definition/local declaration mechanism;
57:    symbol registration never licenses a theorem.
58: 2. A binder inside the current proposition's full statement. Its scope remains
59:    that statement. A variable bound in an input does not become a free object
60:    in the consuming proof; instantiate the statement explicitly.
61: 3. A local declaration before first use, recording its kind, type, exact
62:    declaration, introduction basis, and scope. An arbitrary variable requires
63:    legitimate quantifier introduction; a definition uses already available
64:    objects; a witness requires an input or an earlier local existence proof.
65: 
66: A declaration cannot grant existence, uniqueness, invertibility, regularity,
67: or a desired property merely by naming an object. Those obligations require
68: proof. Any D guard needed to use the object must be a direct R input, not a
69: theorem silently recovered from ancestor closure. Record mutually compatible
70: choices and witness dependence. Temporary assumptions stay inside R and must
71: be correctly discharged. Branch witnesses, local facts and local notation
72: cannot escape their scopes. Export a quantified or conditional statement when
73: needed, rather than a free private name. Global names are reserved; dummy
74: variables may be reused in disjoint local scopes.
75: 
76: ## Dependency closure
77: 
78: Inventory actual factual uses from the prose back to their grounds, not just
79: from an input list forward to a generic `uses` list. Each substantive imported theorem, prior project lemma or original
80: assumption must be a direct input. Eligible routine mathematical facts are recorded as mathematical audit notes
81: with actual local grounds, without requiring a native implementation lookup. A definition supplies meaning, not a theorem. An R output is not its
82: own premise. Adding the desired formula as an unproved input is not a repair.
83: 
84: Explicit local calculations and fully proved intermediate facts may remain
85: inside R. Give a reused local fact a full F statement and identify its earlier
86: derivation and open assumptions. No separate graph vertex is needed for every
87: algebraic equality. A nontrivial imported result cannot be called a local
88: calculation. Substantive reusable lemmas should become N/R pairs; any fact
89: reused by another R must be exported in a complete proposition statement.
90: 
91: The controller owns `spec.logic.calculations` and the small core syntax table
92: (`nl0/scripts/foundations.py`). The clean author tool binds omitted metadata and
93: rejects extra author permissions or task-specific primitives. This fixed
94: language grants no MVT, FTC, Fubini, convergence, compactness or regularity
95: theorem. Such facts need legitimate explicit inputs, an actual local derivation or
96: eligible positively reviewed mathematical background; the syntax table alone
97: grants none of them.
98: An author-written permission claim, in any field or prose, has no authority.
99: Ordinary typed arithmetic notation is part of this fixed language: natural
100: numbers, integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers mean their standard
101: structures with usual numerals and operations. Finite calculations include
102: their zero/one laws, such as `a+0=a`, as well as explicit algebra/order
103: derivations. Do not demand a separate E/M for an operation token or an allowed
104: finite calculation. This does not grant calculus, topology or measure theorems.
105: Conversely, inspect an actual displayed local derivation before demanding a
106: duplicate E/M input for its conclusion. A named consequence proved by permitted
107: finite algebra/order steps is not an imported premise. If a local derivation
108: fails, locate its unsupported implication rather than its absent theorem name.
109: 
110: Metadata accounts for the argument but never replaces it. Copying all inputs
111: into a single `uses` record, registering a symbol without declaring it in the
112: proof, or writing a PASS label cannot establish closure.
113: 
114: ## Operational acceptance
115: 
116: 1. Author using the node template. Reverse-check the actual prose for missing
117:    declarations, unexpanded references and unlisted facts before freezing.
118: 2. Generate a packet for each R. The v2 generator supplies no original proof,
119:    producer proofs, provenance file locators, extra ancestor statements or
120:    undeclared ambient H. Direct source contracts and required definitions are
121:    included. Packet hashes bind the mathematical input actually reviewed.
122: 3. Review all closure/inference checks, admitting positively checked routine
123:    background notes under the shared policy. Record concrete packet locations and reasons for every verdict.
124: 4. Perform a fresh local mathematical replay. The reviewer gets the skill instructions
125:    and that packet, without original proof,
126:    other R bodies, author review
127:    notes, old verdicts, or an answer key. Record the actual carrier, packet hash,
128:    prior exposure and mathematical material read. Skill instructions supply no
129:    extra mathematical premise. Do not falsely claim a same-context rereading
130:    is a fresh replay. This rule does not authorize starting a new external
131:    service or agent; if the required carrier has not been used, keep replay
132:    UNVERIFIED and report that limit.
133:    Prior exposure means known task/proof material supplied or read in earlier
134:    contexts; this is not a claim about unknown pretraining contents. Learned
135:    mathematical knowledge cannot replace a missing declared premise or proof.
136: 5. An ineligible missing declaration, missing statement content, unlisted substantive theorem or need
137:    to look outside the packet blocks acceptance. Record the defect; do not
138:    silently repair it while assigning PASS. Return substantive/structural defects to authoring and review the frozen
139:    revision; eligible background notes need no author rewrite. Routine completion does not require a
140:    separate user interruption for every omission. Distinguish a representation
141:    defect from a substantive mathematical gap under the existing gap policy.
142: 
143: The code rejects explicit malformed references, inventories, scopes, guards
144: and receipts. It does not infer hidden hypotheses from property words in types,
145: or decide theorem applications by matching a list of mathematical names.
146: These semantic obligations apply equally to every subject and remain part of
147: author inspection and Audit A. An omitted inventory entry or unnamed
148: theorem hidden in prose still requires actual semantic review. Freshness and
149: truthful reviewer identity need execution evidence; record shape/hashes cannot
150: authenticate them. No natural-language audit is a Lean kernel certificate.

artifact.proof:
We prove the exact full_target with its original assumptions: n is any natural number (zero is allowed), E⊆ℝ^n is nonempty and compact, and I=[0,1]. We model Euclidean ℝ^n by Ambient n=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). The final ambient metric is Euclidean. In the intermediate argument only, X×ℝ carries the maximum product metric d((x,t),(y,u))=max(d_X(x,y),|t−u|). Section 6 proves the required change of metric, with explicit constants. Compactness remains an original hypothesis; the new argument happens to prove the result for all nonempty subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space and so does not need compactness.

Definitions and normalization. All measure values and countable sums of nonnegative costs may lie in [0,∞]. For s>0 define C_s(δ,A)=Content(s,ofReal δ,A), for real δ>0, using the countable-cover infimum in lean_header. Define H^s(A)=μH[s](A), Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure. For positive s the guard sup_{U_i nonempty} (ediam U_i)^s in that formula is exactly (ediam U_i)^s: the only difference could occur for an empty U_i, whose diameter and positive power are both zero. Thus the definitions agree with the unnormalized countable-cover definitions in problem.md, not a normalized spherical measure. We never need the exponent-zero measure. Hausdorff dimension is Mathlib dimH with values in [0,∞]; by B002 this has the stipulated critical-exponent meaning. The final dimensions are finite by B004 and the proved upper bound. Accordingly their equality in [0,∞] is the original real-valued equality as well.

§1. Derivation of B101 (cover content and positive budgets).
For each s>0 the preceding guard observation identifies C_s with the raw cover infimum. If 0<δ₁≤δ₂, every δ₁-cover is also a δ₂-cover, hence C_s(δ₂,A)≤C_s(δ₁,A). B001 says H^s is the supremum over all positive extended scales. The same supremum is obtained from finite positive real scales: those are included in all extended scales, and every positive extended scale r admits a finite positive real δ with ofReal δ≤r, so its content is bounded by the content at δ. These observations prove both the identification and the stated supremum formula.

Now let q>0, H^q(A)=0, r>0 and ε>0. The content at r/2 is zero. By the defining property of the infimum there is a countable cover U_i with ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2) and total q-cost <ofReal(ε/4). In particular all diameters are finite. Write d_i=(ediam U_i).toReal, so 0≤d_i≤r/2 and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i. For each i put e_i=ε·2^(−i−3), with i starting at zero, so e_i>0 and Σ_i e_i=ε/4. By B010, continuity of x↦x^q at d_i and the strict gap d_i<r allow a choice a_i with d_i<a_i≤r and a_i^q<d_i^q+e_i. To be explicit, take η_i>0 sufficiently small that η_i<r−d_i and |(d_i+η_i)^q−d_i^q|<e_i, and put a_i=d_i+η_i. Such choices are independent for each natural index. Empty covering members are harmless and receive their own positive numerical budgets. Summing nonnegative inequalities gives Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)≤Σ_i ofReal(d_i^q)+ofReal(ε/4)<ofReal(ε/2)<ofReal ε. The geometric series identity follows by summing its first m terms, (ε/4)(1−2^(−m)), and letting m tend to infinity. No positive diameter of an actual set is required. This proves B101, including for a zero-dimensional or singleton space.

§2. Derivation of B102 (slicing inequality).
Fix any metric space X, subset A, s>0 and finite δ>0. Let V_i be any countable δ-cover of A×I in the maximum product metric. Empty V_i will contribute zero throughout; all hulls and weights mentioned below are assigned the empty set and zero for such indices. For a nonempty V_i write ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal∈[0,δ], A_i=π_X(V_i), and B_i=π_ℝ(V_i). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz, because each coordinate distance is bounded by the maximum distance. B011 therefore gives ediam A_i≤ofReal ρ_i and ediam B_i≤ofReal ρ_i.

The nonempty real set B_i is bounded: choose t_i∈B_i, and then every t∈B_i satisfies |t−t_i|≤ρ_i; this uses the definition of diameter and its finiteness. Let J_i=[inf B_i,sup B_i]. B009 gives B_i⊆J_i and volume(J_i)=ediam B_i≤ofReal ρ_i. Each J_i is closed and measurable, although B_i and V_i need not be measurable. Empty V_i have J_i=∅ as stipulated.

Fix t∈I. The sets A_i with t∈J_i cover A: for each x∈A, choose a cover member containing (x,t); it is nonempty and gives x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. Represent this subfamily as the natural-indexed cover W_i(t)=A_i when t∈J_i, and ∅ otherwise. Its members have diameter≤δ and their s-costs are bounded by ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t). The definition of C_s therefore gives
    c:=C_s(δ,A) ≤ Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i}(t)  for every t∈I.
Outside I use zero on both sides by multiplying every indicator by 1_I. Thus on all ℝ,
    c1_I ≤ Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s)1_{J_i∩I}.
All functions on the right are measurable, since J_i∩I is a Borel set, and all weights are finite nonnegative real powers. The same applies to the left even when c=∞. Apply B008 to this pointwise inequality, B006 to the nonnegative series with Lebesgue measure on ℝ, and B007 to each measurable indicator. Since volume(I)=1 by B009 and volume(J_i∩I)≤volume(J_i) by measure monotonicity, the result is
    c = c·1 ≤ Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) volume(J_i∩I)
      ≤ Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^s) ofReal ρ_i
       = Σ_i ofReal(ρ_i^(s+1)).
The power identity holds for ρ_i>0 by real powers and for ρ_i=0 because both s and s+1 are positive. For empty indices both sides of the summand are zero. Measure monotonicity applies to every set and needs no additional regularity. All displayed operations are in [0,∞], where multiplication of these finite weights is well-defined, including the zero weights; no subtraction of infinities occurs. In particular no finiteness of c is needed.

This proves c≤cost(V) for every δ-cover. Taking the infimum over V yields C_s(δ,A)≤C_{s+1}(δ,A×I). Taking the supremum over finite positive δ, B101 gives H^s(A)≤H^(s+1)(A×I). This proves B102. The exact inequality has constant one in the maximum product metric, with no compactness assumption.

§3. Derivation of B103 (upper cover).
Suppose q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix a target scale δ>0 and an arbitrary ε>0. Apply B101 with r=min(1,δ)>0 to obtain U_i covering A and budgets 0<a_i≤r, with ediam U_i≤ofReal a_i and Σ a_i^q<ε in the extended-nonnegative interpretation. Define the integer N_i=ceil(1/a_i). Because 0<a_i≤1, N_i≥1, 1/N_i≤a_i, and
    N_i≤1/a_i+1≤2/a_i.
Cover I by the N_i closed intervals J_ij=[j/N_i,(j+1)/N_i], 0≤j<N_i. For every U_i and each such interval, distances between two points of U_i×J_ij are at most max(a_i,1/N_i)≤a_i. Hence its diameter in the maximum metric is at most a_i≤δ. The products cover A×I, and their indexing set {(i,j):i∈ℕ,0≤j<N_i} is countable: it injects into ℕ×ℕ, which is enumerated by successive finite diagonals. Reindex as a sequence, padding by empty sets if needed; the sum of nonnegative costs is unchanged. Their total (q+1)-cost is bounded by
    Σ_i N_i a_i^(q+1) ≤ Σ_i (2/a_i)a_i^(q+1)
      =2 Σ_i a_i^q <2ε.
The only division is by positive a_i, and the power identity is valid for every real q>0. This bound holds for every ε>0 at fixed δ, so the content C_{q+1}(δ,A×I)=0. B101 now gives H^(q+1)(A×I)=0. This proves B103 with the absolute factor 2; it does not depend on dimension or any choice of ambient box. Unlike the supplied upper argument, it applies without a separate n=0 branch.

§4. Derivation of B104 (nonempty slice).
If A is nonempty choose x₀∈A. For all t,u∈ℝ the maximum metric gives d((x₀,t),(x₀,u))=max(0,|t−u|)=|t−u|. Thus f(t)=(x₀,t) is 1-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz. B003 implies dimH(f(I))=dimH I=1, the last equality being B005. Since f(I)⊆A×I, dimension monotonicity gives dimH(A×I)≥1. Let A be nonempty with finite Hausdorff dimension D. Regard D as a finite nonnegative real number; coercing it back to [0,∞] recovers dimH A. Put F=A×I. For every real q>D we have q>0. B002 gives H^q(A)=0. B103 gives H^(q+1)(F)=0, and B002 gives dimH F≤q+1 because zero is not infinity. This also proves dimH F is finite by taking, for example, q=D+1. Letting q decrease to D gives dimH F≤D+1: explicitly if the finite real number dimH F were >D+1, take q=D+(dimH F−D−1)/2, which contradicts dimH F≤q+1.

For the reverse direction, B104 gives dimH F≥1. If D=0 this is already ≥D+1. If D>0, fix any 0<s<D. B002 gives H^s(A)=∞. B102 gives H^(s+1)(F)=∞, and B002 then gives dimH F≥s+1. artifact.proof:
We prove the exact full_target with its original assumptions: n is any natural number (zero is allowed), E⊆ℝ^n is nonempty and compact, and I=[0,1]. We model Euclidean ℝ^n by Ambient n=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). The final ambient metric is Euclidean. In the intermediate argument only, X×ℝ carries the maximum product metric d((x,t),(y,u))=max(d_X(x,y),|t−u|). Section 6 proves the required change of metric, with explicit constants. Compactness remains an original hypothesis; the new argument happens to prove the result for all nonempty subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space and so does not need compactness.

Definitions and normalization. All measure values and countable sums of nonnegative costs may lie in [0,∞]. For s>0 define C_s(δ,A)=Content(s,ofReal δ,A), for real δ>0, using the countable-cover infimum in lean_header. Define H^s(A)=μH[s](A), Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure. For positive s the guard sup_{U_i nonempty} (ediam U_i)^s in that formula is exactly (ediam U_i)^s: the only difference could occur for an empty U_i, whose diameter and positive power are both zero. Thus the definitions agree with the unnormalized countable-cover definitions in problem.md, not a normalized spherical measure. We never need the exponent-zero measure. Hausdorff dimension is Mathlib dimH with values in [0,∞]; by B002 this has the stipulated critical-exponent meaning. The final dimensions are finite by B004 and the proved upper bound. Accordingly their equality in [0,∞] is the original real-valued equality as well.

§1. Derivation of B101 (cover content and positive budgets).
For each s>0 the preceding guard observation identifies C_s with the raw cover infimum. If 0<δ₁≤δ₂, every δ₁-cover is also a δ₂-cover, hence C_s(δ₂,A)≤C_s(δ₁,A). B001 says H^s is the supremum over all positive extended scales. The same supremum is obtained from finite positive real scales: those are included in all extended scales, and every positive extended scale r admits a finite positive real δ with ofReal δ≤r, so its content is bounded by the content at δ. These observations prove both the identification and the stated supremum formula.

Now let q>0, H^q(A)=0, r>0 and ε>0. The content at r/2 is zero. By the defining property of the infimum there is a countable cover U_i with ediam U_i≤ofReal(r/2) and total q-cost <ofReal(ε/4). In particular all diameters are finite. Write d_i=(ediam U_i).toReal, so 0≤d_i≤r/2 and ediam U_i=ofReal d_i. For each i put e_i=ε·2^(−i−3), with i starting at zero, so e_i>0 and Σ_i e_i=ε/4. By B010, continuity of x↦x^q at d_i and the strict gap d_i<r allow a choice a_i with d_i<a_i≤r and a_i^q<d_i^q+e_i. To be explicit, take η_i>0 sufficiently small that η_i<r−d_i and |(d_i+η_i)^q−d_i^q|<e_i, and put a_i=d_i+η_i. Such choices are independent for each natural index. Empty covering members are harmless and receive their own positive numerical budgets. Summing nonnegative inequalities gives Σ_i ofReal(a_i^q)≤Σ_i ofReal(d_i^q)+ofReal(ε/4)<ofReal(ε/2)<ofReal ε. The geometric series identity follows by summing its first m terms, (ε/4)(1−2^(−m)), and letting m tend to infinity. No positive diameter of an actual set is required. This proves B101, including for a zero-dimensional or singleton space.

§2. Derivation of B102 (slicing inequality).
Fix any metric space X, subset A, s>0 and finite δ>0. Let V_i be any countable δ-cover of A×I in the maximum product metric. Empty V_i will contribute zero throughout; all hulls and weights mentioned below are assigned the empty set and zero for such indices. For a nonempty V_i write ρ_i=(ediam V_i).toReal∈[0,δ], A_i=π_X(V_i), and B_i=π_ℝ(V_i). Coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz, because each coordinate distance is bounded by the maximum distance. B011 therefore gives ediam A_i≤ofReal ρ_i and ediam B_i≤ofReal ρ_i.

The nonempty real set B_i is bounded: choose t_i∈B_i, and then every t∈B_i satisfies |t−t_i|≤ρ_i; this uses the definition of diameter and its finiteness. Let J_i=[inf B_i,sup B_i]. B009 gives B_i⊆J_i and volume(J_i)=ediam B_i≤ofReal ρ_i. Each J_i is closed and measurable, although B_i and V_i need not be measurable. Empty V_i have J_i=∅ as stipulated.

Fix t∈I. The sets A_i with t∈J_i cover A: for each x∈A, choose a cover member containing (x,t); it is nonempty and gives x∈A_i and t∈B_i⊆J_i. §3. Derivation of B103 (upper cover).
Suppose q>0 and H^q(A)=0. Fix a target scale δ>0 and an arbitrary ε>0. The products cover A×I, and their indexing set {(i,j):i∈ℕ,0≤j<N_i} is countable: it injects into ℕ×ℕ, which is enumerated by successive finite diagonals. §4. Derivation of B104 (nonempty slice).
If A is nonempty choose x₀∈A. For all t,u∈ℝ the maximum metric gives d((x₀,t),(x₀,u))=max(0,|t−u|)=|t−u|. Thus f(t)=(x₀,t) is 1-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz. B003 implies dimH(f(I))=dimH I=1, the last equality being B005. Since f(I)⊆A×I, dimension monotonicity gives dimH(A×I)≥1. To obtain that monotonicity from the precise bundled B003, instantiate B003 on the product space with its identity map and constants 1. This proves B104.

§5. Derivation of B105 (dimension equality in the maximum metric).
Let A be nonempty with finite Hausdorff dimension D. Regard D as a finite nonnegative real number; coercing it back to [0,∞] recovers dimH A. Put F=A×I. For every real q>D we have q>0. B002 gives H^q(A)=0. B103 gives H^(q+1)(F)=0, and B002 gives dimH F≤q+1 because zero is not infinity. This also proves dimH F is finite by taking, for example, q=D+1. Letting q decrease to D gives dimH F≤D+1: explicitly if the finite real number dimH F were >D+1, take q=D+(dimH F−D−1)/2, which contradicts dimH F≤q+1.

For the reverse direction, B104 gives dimH F≥1. If D=0 this is already ≥D+1. If D>0, fix any 0<s<D. B002 gives H^s(A)=∞. B102 gives H^(s+1)(F)=∞, and B002 then gives dimH F≥s+1. If dimH F<D+1, choose a positive s with max(0,dimH F−1)<s<D, possible since D>0 and dimH F−1<D. Then dimH F<s+1, contradiction. Thus dimH F≥D+1 in every case. This proves B105 with precisely the finite-D hypothesis, and without assuming D>0.

§6. Derivation of B106 (Euclidean metric bridge).
Use the object appendCoord n defined in lean_header: appendCoord n (x,t) has first n coordinates x_i and last coordinate t. Every y∈Ambient(n+1) has unique preimage (x,t) where x_i=y_i at the first n coordinates and t=y_last. The function Fin.lastCases in the definition implements exactly this coordinate splitting. For p=(x,t), p′=(x′,t′), put a=‖x−x′‖₂≥0 and b=|t−t′|≥0. Splitting the finite sum of squares of the n+1 coordinate differences gives
    d₂(appendCoord n p,appendCoord n p′)^2
       = Σ_{i<n}|x_i−x′_i|²+|t−t′|²=a²+b².
Since max(a,b)²≤a²+b²≤2max(a,b)², taking nonnegative square roots gives
    d_max(p,p′)≤d₂(appendCoord n p,appendCoord n p′)
       ≤√2 d_max(p,p′).
Thus appendCoord n is √2-Lipschitz and 1-antilipschitz, with constants independent of n and of E. The argument includes n=0: the empty coordinate sum equals zero, x is the unique point of Ambient 0, and the last coordinate remains unchanged. No appeal to an unspecified norm-invariance theorem is needed.
